extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and litigators who practice before the PTAB
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary of terminology and practice standards used in PTAB proceedings under the AIA, with definitions, procedural rules, evidentiary standards, and practice guidance for filing petitions, motions, discovery, and trial before the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: any Discovery beyond Routine Discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTAB will consider the Garmin Factors when determining whether a Motion for Additional Discovery should be granted. In IPR and CBM review, Additional Discovery may be granted in the interest of justice, considering the totality of the circumstances. 37 C.F.R. § 42.51(b)(2)(i). In PGR, Additional Discovery may be granted upon a showing of good cause (a slightly lower standard) and requires the requesting party to establish a specific factual reason for the Additional Discovery. 37 C.F.R. § 42.224.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Patent Judge (APJ)
rubrics_metrics.description: an administrative law judge sitting on the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each APJ is a lawyer, typically with a technical background and many years of experience in patent law, such as in Examination, Patent Prosecution or litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: see Claim Amendment(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: America Invents Act/Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: a federal statute signed into law on September 16, 2011 that changed US patent law, including creating the PTAB and establishing the new PTAB Proceedings of IPR, PGR and CBM review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIA changed the US patent system from a First to Invent system to a First to File system. Pub. L. No. 112-29, 125 Stat. 284-341.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: a Ground of Invalidity or ground for rejecting a patent claim based on the prior invention or disclosure of the claimed invention by another, or the inventor’s own disclosure of the claimed invention by publication, Prior Sale or Prior Use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipation requires that all claim elements appear in a single prior art reference. Anticipation also means a lack of Novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal, Right of
rubrics_metrics.description: both parties to a PTAB Proceeding, the Petitioner and the Patent Owner, may appeal a Final Written Decision of the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All appeals from PTAB Proceedings are made directly to the Federal Circuit. Notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit is due within 63 days of a Final Written Decision. 35 U.S.C. §§ 141-142; 37 C.F.R. § 90.3. The PTAB’s decision to not Institute Trial is final and non-appealable; a Request for Rehearing may be filed within 30 days of the Institution Decision. 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d). Both parties also have a statutory right to seek a Stay of Litigation of pending district court litigation. For CBM review, parties have the right to seek immediate interlocutory, de novo review of a district court’s decision to grant or deny a Stay of Litigation. Pub. L. No. 112-29 § 18(b)(2), 125 Stat. 284-341.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asserted Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: a patent that a Patent Owner enforces, typically by filing suit or threatening to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (BPAI)
rubrics_metrics.description: before September 16, 2012, the BPAI was the adjudicative body within the PTO that focused on patent disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIA replaced the BPAI with the newly formed PTAB. 35 U.S.C. § 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: the Claim Construction standard which applies in PTAB Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim terms are given their BRI in light of the specification to one having ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention. In contrast, in federal district court, claims are construed under the Ordinary and Customary Meaning Standard (Phillips Standard). 37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b). PTAB published a proposed rule change (Aug 20, 2015) to apply Ordinary and Customary Meaning for patents that will expire before issuance of a final decision, but otherwise to apply BRI to unexpired patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: the evidentiary standard to legally establish a fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In PTAB Proceedings, the Petitioner must prove Invalidity of the challenged claims by a Preponderance of the Evidence. 37 C.F.R. § 42.1(d). In contrast, in federal district court the accused infringer must prove Invalidity by Clear and Convincing Evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central Reexamination Unit (CRU)
rubrics_metrics.description: a dedicated unit within the PTO that administers Ex Parte Reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU was formed in 2005 and remains largely unchanged by the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: after the PTAB issues a Final Written Decision and the time for appeal has ended, the PTO issues and publishes a Certificate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate (1) cancels any patent claim determined to be unpatentable, (2) confirms any patent claim determined to be patentable, and (3) incorporates any new or Amended Claim determined to be patentable. 35 U.S.C. § 318(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charged with Infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: a requirement for CBM review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Petition for CBM review may only be filed if the Petitioner, Real Party-in-Interest or Privy has been Charged with Infringement, i.e., there is a real and substantial controversy of the patent such that the party would have standing to bring a Declaratory Judgment action in federal court. This includes being served with a patent infringement complaint. 37 C.F.R. § 42.302(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Amendment(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: after Institution of a PTAB Proceeding and conferring with the PTAB, a Patent Owner may file a Motion to Amend patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Owner may generally propose one Substitute Claim for each original claim it wishes to amend, which will only be considered if the original claim it replaces is canceled by the Patent Owner. A Claim Amendment will not be allowed if it does not respond to all Grounds of Invalidity asserted against the original claim, if it seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims, or if it introduces new subject matter. The Patent Owner must also show patentability of a Substitute Claim over the prior art generally, not just over references asserted against the original claims. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.121, 42.221.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Chart
rubrics_metrics.description: typically a two-column chart providing an element-by-element breakdown of a patent’s claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity claim charts are useful for visualizing which claim elements exist in the prior art. Claim Charts may be single-spaced under Line Spacing requirements, but placing arguments and claim construction in a claim chart to circumvent double-spacing or Page Limits is prohibited. The PTAB will not consider such arguments and double-spaced Claim Constructions. 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(2)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: the process an adjudicative body undergoes to determine the legal meaning of a patent claim term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB gives claim terms their Broadest Reasonable Interpretation, whereas district courts give claim terms their Ordinary and Customary Meaning. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.100(b), 42.200(b), 42.300(b). Proposed rule change (Aug 20, 2015) regarding application of Ordinary and Customary Meaning for certain expiring patents is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and Convincing Evidence/Clear and Convincing Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: the Standard of Proof required to establish the Invalidity of a patent in district court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove Invalidity by Clear and Convincing Evidence, a party must prove that it is substantially more likely than not that the patent is invalid. This standard is higher than the Preponderance of the Evidence standard required in PTAB Proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: if multiple matters before the PTAB involve the same patent (Related Matters), a party may request that the PTAB Consolidate the matters into a single proceeding (Unified Case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a Consolidation, a party seeks PTAB authorization to file a Motion for Joinder. If granted, parties must appoint a Lead Counsel and Speak with a Single Voice in all matters in the Unified Case. 37 C.F.R. § 42.122.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel, Back-up
rubrics_metrics.description: each party in a PTAB Proceeding must be represented by an attorney designated as Lead Counsel and by at least one other attorney designated as Back-up Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back-up Counsel must be able to represent the party before the PTAB on behalf of Lead Counsel, and if not admitted to practice before the PTAB may be admitted Pro Hac Vice. Each party must file a Power of Attorney when designating counsel, except a Patent Owner need not file an additional Power of Attorney if the designated counsel is already counsel of record. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel, Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: each party in a review proceeding must be represented by one attorney who is designated as Lead Counsel and by at least one other attorney designated as Back-up Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead Counsel must be a registered patent attorney. Power of Attorney filing requirements apply as with Back-up Counsel. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method (CBM)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM review is a PTAB Proceeding to challenge any patent that includes at least one claim directed to a method or apparatus used in the practice, administration or management of a Financial Product or Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM review is not available for patents for Technological Inventions. 37 C.F.R. § 42.301(a). CBM review may be requested on the basis of Novelty, Obviousness, Written Description, Enablement, Indefiniteness and Patentable Subject Matter. All prior art is available when challenging FTF patents; for FTI patents only patents and Printed Publications are considered. 37 C.F.R. § 42.304. Only a person who is sued or Charged with Infringement may Petition for CBM review. 37 C.F.R. § 42.302. Timing: may be requested at any time for FTI patents, but for FTF patents only nine months after issuance for petitions analogous to PGR window. 37 C.F.R. § 42.303.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: a written statement submitted to the PTAB, often providing factual or expert testimony (an Expert Declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declarant must attest that all statements of own knowledge are true and that statements on information and belief are believed to be true. 37 C.F.R. § 1.68. Willful false statements are punishable. Uncompelled direct testimony must be submitted as a Declaration; all other testimony must be in deposition transcript form. 37 C.F.R. § 42.53(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: a legal determination by a court resolving an issue affecting the rights of the parties to a dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common in patent litigation, it allows alleged infringers to seek judicial determination of Validity, non-infringement, or enforceability before the Patent Owner sues. A Declaratory Judgment action may allow the alleged infringer to determine the forum of the lawsuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Protective Order
rubrics_metrics.description: a form Protective Order provided in the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide that is automatically entered if the parties do not agree on a Protective Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.55. On Aug 20, 2015 PTAB proposed revising the form Protective Order to place the burden on the designating party to show good cause to seal “confidential” information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrative/Demonstrative Exhibit
rubrics_metrics.description: materials, typically visual, used during oral argument before the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstratives are allowed but strictly limited. Testimony not previously developed in papers may not be discussed for the first time in a Demonstrative Exhibit at oral hearing. The presenting party bears the burden of showing the material does not present new argument or Evidence. Demonstratives must be served at least five business days before oral argument and filed no later than the time of oral argument. 37 C.F.R. § 42.70(b). Proposed rule change (Aug 20, 2015) extended exchange to seven business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation Proceeding (DER)
rubrics_metrics.description: a form of inter partes proceeding designed to resolve inventorship disputes for FTF patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a DER, a Petitioner with a pending patent application seeks to establish that an earlier filed application on the same invention was derived from Petitioner’s application and is not entitled to Priority. FTI patent applications remain subject to Interference Proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: a Patent Owner’s voluntary cancellation of a claim in a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer is a statutory right and does not invalidate remaining claims that do not depend on the disclaimed claim. 35 U.S.C. § 253(a). A Petition for PTAB Proceedings will not be Instituted based on disclaimed claims. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.107(e), 42.207(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: while Discovery in PTAB Proceedings is generally limited, parties are entitled to Mandatory Initial Disclosures and Routine Discovery. Any Discovery beyond Routine Discovery is considered Additional Discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree to Additional Discovery, or a party may file a Motion for Additional Discovery. 37 C.F.R. § 42.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: a requirement for patentability and distinct from the Written Description requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To satisfy Enablement, a patent specification must contain sufficient information such that a person of ordinary skill in the art could make or use the invention from the disclosures in the patent together with information known in the art without undue experimentation. 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). Enablement may be raised as a Ground of Invalidity in PGR and CBM review, but not in IPR. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.104(b)(2), 42.204(b)(2), 42.304(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: a doctrine prohibiting a party, Real Party-in-Interest, or Privy to a district court litigation or PTAB Proceeding from asserting certain Grounds of Invalidity in a later proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For PTAB Proceedings, Estoppel only applies after the PTAB has issued a Final Written Decision. 37 C.F.R. § 42.73(d). In district court litigation, Estoppel applies after the court has entered a final judgment. The Scope of Estoppel depends on the type of PTAB Proceeding and is further described under 'Estoppel, Scope of.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel, Scope of
rubrics_metrics.description: the Grounds of Invalidity a party is prohibited from raising in a later proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory Estoppel applies to IPR, PGR and CBM under the AIA. For IPR or PGR, the Petitioner, Real Party-in-Interest or Privy is estopped from asserting in any later proceeding any Ground of Invalidity that Petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during the PTAB Proceeding. 35 U.S.C. §§ 315(e), 325(e). For CBM, estoppel differs by later proceeding: for later PTAB Proceedings, a CBM Petitioner is estopped from asserting any Ground raised or reasonably could have raised; for later district court litigation, estoppel applies only to Grounds actually asserted by the CBM Petitioner. Limited statutory estoppel applies to district court litigation under AIA regarding Declaratory Judgment filers. Additional notes on interplay with district court judgments and PTAB findings are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: includes Declarations, transcripts of depositions and other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Evidence submitted in PTAB Proceedings must be filed in the form of an Exhibit. 37 C.F.R. § 42.63. Except as otherwise provided, the Federal Rules of Evidence apply to PTAB Proceedings. 37 C.F.R. § 42.62(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: a proceeding conducted between the Patent Owner and the PTO to review the patentability of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Owner or a third party may request Ex Parte Reexamination of an issued patent based on other patents and Printed Publications. The requesting party must submit prior art establishing a “substantial new question of patentability” based on Novelty or Obviousness. If granted, the PTO begins reexamination proceedings before the CRU and third-party requesters are excluded from proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: the procedure by which the PTO reviews a patent application, interacts with applicants and their representatives and determines whether the claims are patentable over the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit
rubrics_metrics.description: all Evidence submitted in PTAB Proceedings must be filed in the form of an Exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit List
rubrics_metrics.description: in PTAB Proceedings, each party is required to maintain an Exhibit List with the Exhibit Number and a brief description of each Exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an Exhibit is not filed, the Exhibit List should note that. A current Exhibit List must be served when Evidence is served, and the current Exhibit List must be filed when Exhibits are filed. 37 C.F.R. § 42.63(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit Number
rubrics_metrics.description: in PTAB Proceedings, each party’s Exhibits must be uniquely numbered sequentially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Petitioner, the range is 1001-1999, and for the Patent Owner, the range is 2001-2999. 37 C.F.R. § 42.63(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Declaration/Report
rubrics_metrics.description: a written statement by an expert setting forth his or her analysis and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Expert Declaration is permissible and often helpful as an attachment to a Petition, especially for complex technologies. PTAB discourages incorporating Expert Declarations by reference. Expert testimony that does not disclose underlying facts or data is entitled to little or no weight. Testimony on US patent law or Patent Examination will not be admitted. 37 C.F.R. § 42.65. Analysis of Grounds of Invalidity must appear in the body of a Petition and may contain pinpoint citations to an Expert Declaration. Expert Declarations may be any length but generally should be limited to less than 100 pages and cannot be used to extend Petition length or circumvent Page Limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Circuit/Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit Final
rubrics_metrics.description: Written Decisions are appealable directly to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, which has exclusive jurisdiction over appeals for PTAB Proceedings and patent litigations in federal district court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: rules governing the conduct of all civil actions in federal district courts, including patent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Rules of Civil Procedure do not govern PTAB Proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Rules of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: rules governing Evidence in federal district courts, including patent litigation, as well as in PTAB Proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Date (for a Petition)
rubrics_metrics.description: the date officially accorded to a filed Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Filing Date is assigned on the date the Petitioner: (1) satisfies the requirement for Content of the Petition, (2) effects service on the Patent Owner and (3) submits the appropriate Filing Fee for that PTAB Proceeding. 37 C.F.R. § 42.106. If Petition complies with statutory requirements, original submission date is the Filing Date; no Filing Date will be assigned if statutory requirements not satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: fees due when filing a Petition for PTAB Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR filing: request fee $9,000 plus $200 per claim over 20 and post-Institution fee $14,000 plus $400 per claim over 15. PGR/CBM filing: request fee $12,000 plus $250 per claim over 20 and post-Institution fee $18,000 plus $550 per claim over 15. DER filing fee $400. 37 C.F.R. § 42.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Times
rubrics_metrics.description: a Motion may only be filed according to a schedule set by the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of a schedule, an Opposition filing is due one month after service of a Motion and a Reply filing is due one month after service of the Opposition. 37 C.F.R. § 42.25. For PTAB Proceedings generally: Patent Owner Preliminary Response due within three months after Petition filed; Institution Decision within three months; scheduling order issued; proceeding concludes within 12 months (may be extended six months for cause). 37 C.F.R. § 107(b), §§ 42.100, 42.200, 42.300. Patent Owner Response and Motion to Amend claims due within three months of Institution Decision, then Petitioner’s Reply and Opposition to Amendment due three months later; Patent Owner Reply to Opposition to Amendment due one month later. All submissions must be made electronically via PRPS before 12:00am ET.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Written Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: the written order issued by the PTAB after a Judgment in a PTAB Proceeding conducted on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB will generally issue a Final Written Decision within 18-24 months of the Petition’s Filing Date. The Final Written Decision creates Estoppel and the parties’ Right of Appeal. PTAB Proceedings that settle or are never Instituted will not have a Final Written Decision and no Estoppel or Right of Appeal will apply. 37 C.F.R. § 42.73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Product or Service
rubrics_metrics.description: to be eligible for CBM review, the patent at issue must have at least one claim related to a Financial Product or Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB broadly construes Financial Product or Service to include activities financial in nature, incidental to a financial activity or complementary to a financial activity. 37 C.F.R. § 42.301(b). When a patent’s claims relate to money matters or can be performed by a financial institution, the patent likely relates to a Financial Product or Service even if not otherwise related to financial services. A single covered claim can make the entire patent eligible for CBM review. 77 Fed. Reg. at 48736. Examples and PTAB decisions cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: First to File (FTF)
rubrics_metrics.description: a system of granting patents where Priority is given to the first person to file a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 16, 2013 with the AIA, the US transitioned from FTI to FTF. Priority disputes in an FTF system often resolved through DERs.

rubrics_metrics.name: First to Invent (FTI)
rubrics_metrics.description: a system of granting patents where Priority is given to the first person to invent the subject matter of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US used FTI until March 16, 2013. Issued patents claiming Priority before that date are FTI patents. 35 U.S.C. § 100. Priority disputes under FTI often resolved through Interference Proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font
rubrics_metrics.description: petitions and other documents created for a proceeding must be in either a proportional Font that is 14-point or larger or a monospaced Font that does not contain more than four characters per centimeter (10 characters per inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain 14-point proportional Fonts are so narrow they cannot be read easily. When using 14-point proportional Font, parties should select a Font of sufficient width (e.g., Times New Roman). 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(2)(ii). See Petition, Formatting of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garmin Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: factors used by the PTAB to determine whether a Motion for Additional Discovery should be granted (from Garmin Int’l, Inc. v. Cuozzo Speed Techs. LLC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Garmin Factors include: (1) requesting party must establish more than a possibility and mere allegation of finding something useful, (2) litigation positions and underlying bases are not discoverable, (3) requesting party must not have ability to generate equivalent information by other means, (4) requests must be easily understandable, and (5) requests must not be overly burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graham Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: questions of fact used to resolve Obviousness as set forth by the Supreme Court in Graham v. John Deere Co.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graham Factors include: (1) the scope and content of the prior art, (2) the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art, and (3) the level of ordinary skill in the art. Further objective Evidence (Secondary Considerations) may also be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of Invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: the grounds on which a Petitioner can challenge the Validity of patent claims in a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IPR, Grounds limited to Novelty and Obviousness. For PGR and CBM, challenges may include Novelty, Obviousness, Written Description, Enablement, Indefiniteness and Patentable Subject Matter. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.104, 42.204(b), 42.304(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Horizontal Redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: assertion of multiple prior art references that separately and distinctly support the same Ground of Invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PTAB denies Grounds for being redundant, the Petitioner is statutorily estopped from pursuing the grounds in subsequent litigation or further PTAB Proceedings. 35 U.S.C. §§ 315(e), 325(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefiniteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Definiteness is a requirement for patentability; to satisfy Definiteness, a patent claim must particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indefiniteness is available as a Ground of Invalidity in PGR and CBM review, but not IPR. 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.104(b), 42.204(b), 42.304(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informative Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: a Final Written Decision designated as particularly instructive by a majority of the APJs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informative Decisions are not binding but are meant to illustrate PTAB principles and reasoning for the public, patent examining corps and future PTAB panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: granting of a Petition for a PTAB Proceeding after considering the Petition and Patent Owner Preliminary Response, if filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. § 314(b). After Institution, PTAB issues a Scheduling Order under which the proceeding concludes within 12 months (may be extended six months for cause). If a Trial is not Instituted, no Estoppel applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: the PTAB’s decision on whether or not to Institute a Trial — generally issued within six months of the Filing Date of the Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. § 314(b). The Institution Standard depends on the particular PTAB Proceeding. PTAB’s decision to not Institute is final and non-appealable. 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(c). A Request for Rehearing may be filed within 30 days. 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: different Institution Standards apply depending on the type of PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IPR, Petition must demonstrate a reasonable likelihood of prevailing on at least one claim. 35 U.S.C. § 314(a). For PGR and CBM review, Petition must demonstrate either that more likely than not at least one claim is unpatentable, or that the Petition raises an unsettled or novel legal question. 35 U.S.C. § 324.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: a proceeding at the PTO conducted among the Patent Owner, PTO and a third-party requester to review the patentability of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third party may request Inter Partes Reexamination based on patents and Printed Publications showing reasonable likelihood the requester will prevail on at least one claim based on Novelty or Obviousness. If so, PTO orders reexamination before the CRU where Patent Owner and requester engage in comment. Inter Partes Reexamination was replaced by IPR review on Sept 16, 2012 and no longer exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Review (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: a PTAB Proceeding for challenging the Validity of any issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR may be requested on basis of Novelty and Obviousness; only patents and Printed Publications may be used as prior art. 37 C.F.R. § 42.104(b). PTAB will not Institute IPR if Petitioner previously filed a Declaratory Judgment action challenging the patent's Validity; a DJ filed as counterclaim to an infringement suit does not bar IPR. 37 C.F.R. § 42.101. IPR may be requested at any time for FTI patents; for FTF patents only nine months after issuance or later. 37 C.F.R. § 42.102. If Petitioner has been served with a patent infringement complaint, PTAB petition must be filed within one year after service. 35 U.S.C. § 315(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: a proceeding conducted by the CRU to resolve which of several parties first invented an invention commonly claimed in two or more FTI patents or patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interferences are conducted among the PTO and several parties as a form of inter partes proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreter
rubrics_metrics.description: an Interpreter may be used when one of the parties uses foreign language deposition testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The party calling the witness must initiate a conference at least five days before deposition. The offering party must provide the Interpreter's contact details and resume at least five days before. Opposing party may hire a second Interpreter. If Interpreters disagree on the record, PTAB will determine which interpretation should be given more weight. Voir dire not required but objections to qualifications must be made at time of testimony. Further guidelines in cited PTAB decisions (Ariosa Diagnostics v. Isis Innovation Ltd.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: an accused infringer’s rights to avoid infringement for previously lawful activity that later becomes unlawful when claims are substantively Amended during a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIA explicitly provides Intervening Rights may exist for any amended or new claims determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent during IPR, PGR or CBM. 35 U.S.C. § 318(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: if a patent or any of its claims are found not to comply with any prerequisites for obtaining a patent under 35 U.S.C., the patent or its claims are said to be invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB does not presume a patent or its claims are valid, so Petitioner bears lower burden (Preponderance of Evidence) than in district court, where patent presumed valid. In district court, each claim is presumed valid independently; dependent claims presumed valid even if they depend on an invalid claim. 35 U.S.C. § 282. See Invalidity, Standard of Proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity, Standard of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: district courts observe a rebuttable presumption that an issued patent is valid; to invalidate in district court, a defendant must establish Invalidity by Clear and Convincing Evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB does not presume validity and requires only Preponderance of the Evidence to establish Invalidity. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.1(d), 42.20(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: the combination of a second PTAB Proceeding with a first, already-Instituted PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both Patent Owner and Petitioner may request Joinder by a Motion filed no later than one month after Instituting the first Proceeding. For Joinder to be granted, PTAB must determine the second Petition warrants Institution, and Patent Owner’s Preliminary Response must have been submitted or time for response expired. One Year Bar does not apply to a Petition filed concurrently with a Motion for Joinder. APJs have discretion and have denied or granted Motions for Joinder in varying circumstances. 37 C.F.R. § 42.122.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: a group of distinct entities who together file a single Petition for a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB considers Joint Petitioners a single party that must strictly Speak with a Single Voice both in writing and oral representation. Individual arguments or sections in consolidated filings are not allowed. Only one Lead Counsel for joint petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: the PTAB’s Final Written Decision disposing of all issues that were, or reasonably could have been, raised and decided during a PTAB Proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line Spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB imposes specific formatting requirements for filing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double spacing must always be used except for Claim Charts, headings, tables of contents, tables of authorities, indices, signature blocks and certificates of service. Block quotations may be 1.5 spaced, but must be indented from both left and right margins. 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Initial Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: parties may agree to Mandatory Initial Disclosures as set forth in the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must submit any agreement on initial disclosures no later than the filing of the Patent Owner Preliminary Response or expiration of time to file such response. Upon Institution, parties may automatically take Discovery of information identified in Mandatory Initial Disclosures. If parties fail to agree, a party may seek them by Motion. 37 C.F.R. § 42.51(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: both the Petitioner and the Patent Owner must file certain Mandatory Notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices required: (1) identification of each Real Party-in-Interest, (2) identification of related matters, (3) identification of Lead and Back-up Counsel, and (4) identification of service information. Petitioner must file notices with Petition; Patent Owner must file within 21 days of service of Petition. Both must file updated notices within 21 days of change. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins
rubrics_metrics.description: all documents filed in a PTAB Proceeding must include page Margins that measure at least 2.5 centimeters (1 inch) on all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(2)(iv). See Petition, Formatting of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: a request for relief other than by Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Motion must include a statement of the precise relief requested and a full statement of reasons. A Motion may include a statement of material facts. 37 C.F.R. § 42.22. Generally PTAB requires authorization before filing any Motion; Motions will not be entered without Board authorization. 37 C.F.R. § 42.20(b). Most Motions require prior authorization via conference call, but Motions to Seal and Motions filed with Petitions do not. Motions for Rehearing, Motions to Exclude Evidence and Motions for Observation on Cross-Examination require authorization but are automatically granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion Filing Schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: parties may only file a Motion according to a schedule set by the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default times for acting: an Opposition due one month after service of a Motion; a Reply due one month after service of the Opposition. 37 C.F.R. § 42.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for Observation on Cross-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: a motion for the Petitioner to draw the PTAB’s attention to relevant cross-examination testimony of a reply witness since no further substantive paper is permitted after the Reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Office practice; referenced in guidelines (truncated in source).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: the Standard of Proof required to establish a patent’s Invalidity in PTAB Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove Invalidity by Preponderance, a party must prove it is more likely than not that the patent is invalid. Lower burden than Clear and Convincing Evidence. 37 C.F.R. § 42.1(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: prior art references can be combined to show that a claimed invention is Obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Primary Reference discloses many of the Claim Elements and may be combined with one or more Secondary Reference(s), which disclose other Claim Elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed Publication
rubrics_metrics.description: a reference that has been publicly disseminated or otherwise made available to the extent that it can be located and accessed by persons interested and ordinarily skilled in the subject matter or art exercising reasonable diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: a defense to infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent is invalid if a commercial embodiment was subject to Sale or Offer for Sale more than one year before the patent application was filed. Prior Sale may be raised as a Ground of Invalidity in PGR or CBM review, but not in IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Use
rubrics_metrics.description: a defense to infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent is invalid if the invention was subject to a good faith, public use more than one year before the patent application was filed. Prior Use applies to commercial and non-profit use so long as public is intended beneficiary. Prior Use may be raised in PGR or CBM, but not IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: the date on which an inventor established a right to patent invention — generally the effective filing date of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking patent protection in several countries, WIPO provides that once an application is filed in a member country, the applicant is entitled to claim Priority for 12 months and the filing date of that first application is the Priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy
rubrics_metrics.description: see Real Party-in-Interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Hac Vice
rubrics_metrics.description: counsel may be admitted in a PTAB Proceeding Pro Hac Vice even if counsel is not a registered practitioner before the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Motion for admission Pro Hac Vice must be filed more than 21 days after service of the Petition. An Opposition is due within one week and no Reply should be filed. Motion must contain: (1) statement of facts showing good cause, and (2) a Declaration attesting that counsel (a) is a member in good standing of the Bar, (b) has no suspensions or disbarments, (c) has never had an admission denied, (d) has never been sanctioned or held in contempt, (e) will read the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide and Board’s Rules of Practice for Trials, (f) will be subject to PTO’s Code of Professional Responsibility and (g) has familiarity with subject matter. Declaration must list other PTO Pro Hac Vice admissions in past three years. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10; cited PTAB decision examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Protective Order
rubrics_metrics.description: a Protective Order agreed upon by the parties that differs from the Default Protective Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may submit a Proposed Protective Order to PTAB but must explain how it differs from Default Protective Order and how it complies with Office Patent Trial Practice Guide. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.54, 42.55. Often submitted with a Motion to Seal; opposing party may access filed information by agreeing to Proposed Protective Order terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective Order
rubrics_metrics.description: an agreement between or among the PTAB and the parties which provides details for identifying confidential information and rules governing its disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: a litigation-like process established under the AIA (effective Sept. 16, 2012) for challenging the Validity of issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common proceedings include CBM review, IPR and PGR. A PTAB Proceeding begins when a Petitioner files a Petition and the Trial period begins at Institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party-in-Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: the party who desires Institution of a PTAB Proceeding — generally the Petitioner or a party at its behest and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is highly fact-dependent; considerations include whether a non-party exercises control over a Petitioner’s participation, whether a non-party is funding or directing the proceeding. Petitioners must disclose all Real Parties-in-Interest in Mandatory Notices. Office Patent Trial Practice Guide citations and PTAB decisions referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Likelihood Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: a discretionary standard for Instituting an IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must establish it is more likely than not to prevail as to at least one Ground of Invalidity. 35 U.S.C. § 314(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant Grounds of Invalidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds of Invalidity that are the same or substantially the same as those presented in a previous Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB will not consider Redundant Grounds and will only sustain more than one Ground per claim if Petitioner explains why multiple Grounds are not redundant. Different types: Horizontally Redundant or Vertically Redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: any other judicial or administrative matter that would affect, or be affected by, a decision in a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Pending Civil Action involving same parties or patent, or a patent application claiming priority to the patent. Petitioner must disclose Related Matters in Mandatory Notices. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: a party’s response to any Petition, Motion or Opposition filed by the opposing party in a PTAB Proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Adverse Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: a party’s request for judgment against itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (1) Disclaimer of the challenged patent, (2) cancellation or Disclaimer of a claim such that the party has no remaining claim at trial, (3) concession that the patent is unpatentable or that the contested subject matter is derived from another application, and (4) abandonment of the PTAB Proceeding. Generally used due to recent acquisition, change in Privy, or if Proceeding pending only on subset of claims and Patent Owner does not wish to risk Joinder. 37 C.F.R. § 42.73(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Reconsideration / Request for Rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: a request to reconsider the PTAB’s decision on a Petition or Motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Party filing need not obtain prior authorization but must specifically identify all matters believed misapprehended or overlooked and where each matter was previously addressed. Request to Rehear a Petition for Institution must be filed within 30 days of Institution Decision. 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine Discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery to which parties are automatically entitled in PTAB Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (1) any exhibit cited in a paper or testimony, (2) cross examination of affidavit testimony, and (3) relevant information inconsistent with a position advanced by a party. 37 C.F.R. § 42.51(b)(1). In IPR, Additional Discovery may be granted in interest of justice. 37 C.F.R. § 42.51(b)(2). In PGR and CBM, Motion for Additional Discovery may be granted upon showing of good cause and is limited to Evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party. 37 C.F.R. § 42.224(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11 Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: a proposed rule change that would add a Rule 11-type certification for all papers filed with the Board, with sanctions for noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed in PTAB rule changes published Aug 20, 2015; would apply to practitioners and parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: transfer of a commercial embodiment of a patented invention in return for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Prior Sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling Order
rubrics_metrics.description: an order issued concurrently with an Institution Decision setting due dates for an Instituted Trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scheduling Order will take into account complexity while ensuring Trial is completed within one year statutory Pendency. Practice Guide citations provided. 77 Fed. Reg. 6868, 6869 (Feb. 9, 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: objective Evidence in IPR, PGR and CBM proceedings tending to show that an invention was not Obvious over the asserted prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include commercial success, industry recognition, long-felt but unsolved need, unexpected results and copying by competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: prior art references that can be combined with a Primary Reference to show Obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Primary Reference discloses most Claim Elements. Secondary References disclose other Claim Elements combined with the Primary Reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: an agreement between the parties to a PTAB Proceeding that serves as basis for a Motion to Terminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB is not required to terminate Proceedings based on a Settlement and may proceed to a Final Written Decision regardless. 37 C.F.R. § 42.74.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: formatting rule: all documents filed must use double Spacing for all text except certain enumerated parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Claim Charts, headings, tables of contents, tables of authorities, indices, signature blocks and certificates of service. Block quotations may be 1.5 spaced and must be indented from left and right margins. 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(2)(iii). See Petition, Formatting of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak with a Single Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: in Unified Cases, multiple Petitioners are considered a single party that must Speak with a Single Voice both in writing and oral representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual arguments, submissions or sections in consolidated filings are not allowed. Each Petitioner must allow Lead Counsel to speak on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: the level of Evidence required to establish a particular fact or legal issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depends on issue, Motion and PTAB Proceeding. Two applicable Standards of Proof: Clear and Convincing Evidence and Preponderance of the Evidence. 35 U.S.C. § 316(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of Litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: an order temporarily suspending a Pending Civil Action or concurrent PTO proceeding, often during pendency of a PTAB Proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: a claim proposed by a Patent Owner to replace original claims through Claim Amendment in a Motion to Amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Owner may propose one Substitute Claim per original claim it wishes to amend; each Substitute Claim must be traceable back to an original claim. A Substitute Claim will be considered only if the original claim it replaces is determined unpatentable or cancelled. Proposed Substitute Claim may only narrow the scope and not broaden the challenged claim. Patent Owner required to show proposed new claims are patentable at least over prior art it is aware of. 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.121, 42.221.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiently Final
rubrics_metrics.description: a district court judgment affirmed on appeal that ends the litigation on the merits and leaves nothing for the district court to do but execute the Judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Information
rubrics_metrics.description: information submitted by a Petitioner after Institution of a PTAB Proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must file a Motion for Supplemental Information within one month of the Institution Decision; all Supplemental Information must be relevant to a claim for which the PTAB Proceeding has been Instituted. A Motion for Supplemental Information filed more than one month after Institution must establish the information could not reasonably have been obtained earlier and that consideration would be in the interest of justice. 37 C.F.R. § 42.123.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: a patent is not eligible for CBM review if it claims subject matter that as a whole recites a technological feature that is Novel and Unobvious over the prior art, and solves a technical problem using a technical solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.301; see Transitional Program for Covered Business Method Patents—Definitions of Covered Business Method Patent and Technological Invention, 77 Fed. Reg. 48734, 48753 (Aug. 14, 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial
rubrics_metrics.description: an adversarial process during which parties submit Evidence, depose witnesses, and advocate regarding Invalidity of a challenged patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Trial, PTAB determines Validity. Trial period begins at Institution and continues until PTAB issues a Final Written Decision. Pendency of Trial limited to one year after Institution (may be extended up to six months for good cause). 37 C.F.R. §§ 42.100, 42.2, 42.200(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Case
rubrics_metrics.description: a single PTAB Proceeding consisting of Joint Petitioners or Petitions after a successful Motion for Joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Unified Case, multiple Joint Petitioners make up a single party that must Speak with a Single Voice both in writing and oral representation. Individual arguments or sections in consolidated filings are not allowed. Only one Lead Counsel may represent multiple Joint Petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: see Invalidity (inverse concept).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity, Standard of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: see Invalidity, Standard of Proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical Redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner’s assertion of multiple Grounds of Invalidity for a single claim based on different prior art references without explaining relative strengths and weaknesses of each Ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Ground is rejected for redundancy, Petitioner is statutorily estopped from pursuing the grounds in a later litigation or PTAB Proceeding. Petitioners should determine their strongest Grounds and proceed only with those.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Description
rubrics_metrics.description: a requirement for patentability; to satisfy Written Description, a patent specification must describe the claimed invention in sufficient detail to show one skilled in the art that the inventor possessed the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. § 112(a). Written Description is available as a Ground of Invalidity in PGR and CBM review, but not IPR.
